Any registered New York voter may apply for an absentee or early mail ballot. You can apply online (https://requestballot.vote.nyc/), in person at your local election office, or by designating another person to deliver your application to your local election office for you.

Absentee and early mail ballot applications are due 10 days before the election if you’d like a ballot mailed, or the day before Election Day if you plan to receive your ballot in person. Absentee and early mail ballots must be postmarked by Election Day or submitted in person by 9pm on Election Day to your County Board of Elections Office or polling site.
Ballot curing is when a voter corrects an issue with their ballot, so it can be counted.

For information on federal campaign contributions, please visit Open Secrets (http://www.opensecrets.org).

For information on state campaign contributions, please visit your state's resource (http://www.elections.ny.gov/CampaignFinance.html).
Information on local, state and federal candidates and ballot measures may be available here (https://www.vote411.org/ballot#.UFoDEFHh-Sp).

Early voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election begins on October 24th and ends on November 1st.

Early Voting Starts: 10 days before Election Day

Early Voting Ends: 2 days before Election Day

The next election date can be found here https://www.vote411.org/new-york.

Contact your local Board of Elections (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for more information.
Polling places will be open from 6:00 am to 9:00 pm.

You are a Military or Overseas voter if you are in uniformed services, living overseas OR a spouse or dependent of a uniformed services voter. To get registered and vote, you can utilize Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)

If you have additional questions about elections and voting overseas you can use our state specific elections official directory or contact the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/about-contact)
You can make sure we have safe, fair, and efficient elections for all. Become a poll worker toda (https://powerthepolls.org/lwv)y!

You can find your polling place by utilizing your state resource (https://voterlookup.elections.ny.gov/).

If you have further questions on your polling place location, please contact your local board of elections. (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

New York is a “closed primary” state. In order to vote in the primary election, voters must be registered with a political party. Unaffiliated or independent voters are not able to participate in the primary.

If you have any questions about your state’s primary election, please contact your local election officials (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

Ranked Choice Voting for NYC Local Elections

Currently only New York City uses Ranked Choice Voting for Primary and Special Elections. Voters may rank up to five candidates in order of preference (1st choice, 2nd choice, and so on). You may choose to vote for only one candidate if you prefer, but each candidate may receive only one ranking. For more information, contact the New York City Board of Elections. (https://vote.nyc/RankedChoiceVoting)

Here is what you need to know to register in New York:

There are three methods of voter registration in New York: register in-person, register online (https://elections.ny.gov/voter-registration-process), or mail a printable application (https://elections.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2025/04/2025-vr-form-english-_fillable_.pdf) to your local county board of elections office (https://publicreporting.elections.ny.gov/CountyBoardRoster/CountyBoardRoster).

To verify your voter registration status

  click here!  (https://voterlookup.elections.ny.gov/)
The voter registration deadline for the Tuesday, November 3, 2026 General Election is October 24, 2026.
